data.cultural_impact: The name Regan gained popularity in the English-speaking world through the literary works of William Shakespeare and Frank McCourt. In Shakespeare's "King Lear," Regan is the name of one of the treacherous daughters who betrays her father, illustrating the destructive potential of power. In McCourt's "Angela's Ashes," Regan is the name of a young girl who represents hope and resilience in the face of poverty and hardship. These cultural depictions show the name Regan to be associated with power, leadership, and complexity, making it a compelling choice for parents looking for a strong and meaningful name for their child.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name Regan can be seen as a reminder of the power and responsibility that comes with leadership. As the name implies, a little ruler carries a great deal of influence and responsibility. Therefore, it encourages those named Regan to use their power wisely and justly to benefit those around them and to pursue a life of servant leadership, modeling Jesus' humility and selflessness. It also evokes the idea of regency, or the temporary exercise of power or authority, which can inspire one to make the most of the time and opportunities God gives them to make a positive impact on the world.
